$comment: The allow-list is what lets the unattended loop (loop/run.sh) run WITHOUT
--dangerously-skip-permissions. Keep it tight and explicit rather than widening it;
the deny-list is a backstop, not the policy.
defaultMode 'acceptEdits' is a deliberate autonomy choice for the loop: file edits apply
without a prompt, but every Bash/gh call still has to match the allow-list. Remove it if
you would rather approve each edit.
The skills and the maker/checker agents are NOT here any more — they are the outsystems-loop
plugin, so improvements reach every project instead of being copied once and going stale:
/plugin marketplace add kharloridado/outsystems-loop
/plugin install outsystems-loop@outsystems-loop --scope project
Board-driven mode needed four widenings, each with a reason:
gh api graphql  — Projects v2 has no `gh project` command for converting a draft item
to a real issue, and single-select option ids may not be exposed by
`gh project field-list --format json`. Both need raw GraphQL.
gh api repos/*  — to resolve a repository node id for that conversion. Read-only.
gh pr *         — board-ship opens and squash-merges the PR for an Approved card.
git worktree    — every routine builds in its own worktree so it cannot race an
interactive session (docs/LESSONS.md §4.3).
And one TIGHTENING: `Bash(gh project *)` used to be a blanket grant, which also
permitted `gh project delete` and `gh project field-delete` unattended — the two
commands that can destroy the board. It is now enumerated by subcommand. Changing the
board's lanes is a deliberate human act behind ./.github/migrate-project-status.sh.

$denyComment: A BACKSTOP, not the policy — the allow-list above is the policy. Deny patterns are
matched against the start of the command, so a flag that appears mid-command is NOT
reliably caught: `gh pr merge 12 --admin` very likely does not match the --admin rule
below. The real control for that one is the explicit 'never --admin' instruction in
the board-ship skill; the rule here only catches the flag-first spelling.
